t: A ceremonial city at about 3,850 metres near Lake Titicaca, Tiwanaku dominated the southern Andes between about 500 and 1000.
Raised fields, llama caravans and colonies in warm valleys sustained it, while its Staff God imagery spread across the southern Andes.
The city was abandoned around 1010–1050; recent radiocarbon dating suggests this came before the great drought of the 1100s.
dyk: Divers off the Island of the Sun in Lake Titicaca have recovered Tiwanaku offerings of puma-shaped incense burners and the bones of sacrificed young llamas.
ev: Tiwanaku is founded in the southern Titicaca basin, according to recent radiocarbon modelling
Work begins on the Pumapunku platform
Tiwanaku draws migrants from across the region as its red-slipped pottery spreads
Construction of the Akapana, the largest platform mound of the city, is under way
Burials in the city’s tombs cease and a century of violent deaths begins
Permanent residence ends and the city is rapidly abandoned
Tiwanaku is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List

f.predecessor: Pukará and the Late Formative centres of the Titicaca basin
f.successor: Aymara kingdoms such as the Lupaca Kingdom, the Colla Kingdom and the Pacajes
